B: Hiya. Can you hear me?
A: Yes. Hi. Claire.
B: Rob.
A: My husband's called Rob.
B: Yeah, I've had that one today already. Gemma's husband's a Rob as well. I'm starting to feel a bit common.
A: Ha. It's a very common name, to be fair.
B: Cheers.
A: Is that a cat on your shelf in the picture?
B: Yeah, that's Moss. She sits up there and knocks my pens off.
A: Moss. That's annoying. Our dog's called Moth.
B: You're joking.
A: No. Greyhound. He's scared of the neighbour's cat, so I'm not sure they'd get on.
B: Moss would have him, to be honest. She's tiny but she's vicious. So what do you do?
A: Midday supervisor at a primary school. It's not very interesting. You're the ecology student.
B: Word gets round. Yeah, second year, at Man Met. I was at the council before, admin, and I got bored.
A: That's a better reason than most people have for anything.
B: Ha. It's the honest one, anyway.
A: What do you read? You've got a lot of field guides.
B: Field guides, and a lot of nature writing. Robert Macfarlane, Kathleen Jamie, that kind of thing. Bit of sci-fi when I'm fed up with the real world.
A: Kathleen Jamie's good. Some of the rest of it I find a bit much. Every page someone's having a profound moment about a heron.
B: Yeah, there's a lot of that. Some of them you can tell have never actually got wet.
A: Exactly. I've been trying to find anything decent about the fens, and it's either drainage engineering or some man going misty-eyed about the big skies. There's not much in the middle. I sometimes think I'll write it myself. Probably won't.
B: You should, though. I'd read that. The fens are sort of underrated for birds as well. Ouse Washes in winter, all the swans coming in.
A: I walk out that way with the dog. Whooper swans, are they?
B: Whoopers and Bewick's, yeah, though there's fewer Bewick's now. Are you out there a lot?
A: Most days. It's the only bit of the day nobody's talking to me.
B: Ha. I'll keep this short, then.
A: No, you're fine. You're not doing the cheerful thing, which helps.
B: I'm not really built for the cheerful thing.
A: Good. Have you been to Orkney? I went once and it's the only holiday I've ever actually liked.
B: Not Orkney. Mull, a few times, for the eagles. Orkney's on the list. Hen harriers, all that.
